extra.display_text:
The clerk's pen tapped once against the counter, and something in her posture eased from copyist to business. "Mistress Brenna Hallowell," she said. "Desk clerk, and the one who has to walk you through it, so mind the questions." She pulled a ledger toward her and opened it to a fresh page. "Alaric Red. Spell it for me—R-E-D like the color, I'll assume?" She didn't wait long before dipping her pen. "Registration works so. It costs two silver, once, and that's the whole fee—never again. You sign the roll, we take your measure on the stone, and you start at Novice rank. That's the Guild's standing, lowest rung, and it's what lets you take contracts off that board there." She nodded at the notice board with its pebble-weighted papers. "Don't confuse it with your Power Rank—that's a different thing entirely. Power's what you actually are, F through S. The Guild reads it off you, it can't grant it or take it away. Guild Rank is just our ledger." She set a small square slab of grey stone on the counter, unremarkable except that it hummed very faintly, like a struck tuning fork long since faded to almost nothing. "Hand goes on the stone when the time comes. It does the rest." She glanced at the staff on his back. "You'll be measured for what you are, not for what you carry, so no worrying about that." The dice players by the wall had paused their game; one watched over his shoulder with the flat interest of a man with nothing better to do. "Two silver, and I'll need you to mark the ledger. extra.display_text:
Brenna looked up from her copying when the slip came down on the counter. "Glimmerdeep, is it." She pulled the board's ledger toward her, found the line, and wrote his name beside the entry in a quick, practiced hand. "Academy contract, that one. They want the outer level clear—crystal beetles and mineral slimes, mostly, though the report's a season old, so mind it." She stamped the slip with the Guild's seal, pressed it flat, and held it out. "That's yours. Don't lose it; it's what I close the work against when you come back." She capped the stamp and gave him a look over the counter, the kind a woman gives someone she expects to see again in one piece or not at all. "Grotto's a half-day west of the city, past the quarry road—ask at the west gate and they'll point you. Beetles bite and the slimes eat leather, so mind your boots and your straps." The pen dipped back into the ink. "Come back with the level cleared and the desk pays out. Anything else, you know where I sit." The slip was stiff paper, the antler seal dark blue in its corner, the ink of the terms still sharp: *Clear the Outer Grottos of Glimmerdeep — 90 cp, posted for the Glassmere Academy of Magic.* Outside the hall's open door, Glassmere's morning traffic clattered along—a cart, a dog, someone shouting about a delivery. The west gate lay somewhere down the street, past whatever the day put in the way.

mes:
Brenna looked up from her copying when the slip came down on the counter.

"Glimmerdeep, is it." She pulled the board's ledger toward her, found the line, and wrote his name beside the entry in a quick, practiced hand. "Academy contract, that one. They want the outer level clear—crystal beetles and mineral slimes, mostly, though the report's a season old, so mind it." She stamped the slip with the Guild's seal, pressed it flat, and held it out. "That's yours. Don't lose it; it's what I close the work against when you come back."

She capped the stamp and gave him a look over the counter, the kind a woman gives someone she expects to see again in one piece or not at all.

"Grotto's a half-day west of the city, past the quarry road—ask at the west gate and they'll point you. Beetles bite and the slimes eat leather, so mind your boots and your straps." The pen dipped back into the ink. "Come back with the level cleared and the desk pays out. Anything else, you know where I sit."

The slip was stiff paper, the antler seal dark blue in its corner, the ink of the terms still sharp: *Clear the Outer Grottos of Glimmerdeep — 90 cp, posted for the Glassmere Academy of Magic.*

Outside the hall's open door, Glassmere's morning traffic clattered along—a cart, a dog, someone shouting about a delivery. The west gate lay somewhere down the street, past whatever the day put in the way.
